Map of the Tobol-Irtysh Dialect of the Siberian Tatars, 1965. | image = | imagecaption = }} '''Siberian Tatar''' ({{langx|sty|татарца, тадарца, татарча, тадарча, сибиртатарца, себертатарца|translit=tatartsa, tadartsa, tatarcha, tadarcha, sibirtatartsa, sebertatartsa|label=none}}) is a [[Turkic languages|Turkic language]] spoken by about 140,000 people{{Cite web |title=СИБИРСКО-ТАТАРСКИЙ ЯЗЫК • Большая российская энциклопедия - электронная версия |url=https://old.bigenc.ru/linguistics/text/3660444 |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=old.bigenc.ru}} in [[Western Siberia]], [[Russia]], primarily in the oblasts of [[Tyumen Oblast|Tyumen]], [[Novosibirsk Oblast|Novosibirsk]], [[Omsk Oblast|Omsk]], [[Tomsk Oblast|Tomsk]] and [[Kemerovo Oblast|Kemerovo]] Oblasts, but also in [[Sverdlovsk Oblast|Sverdlovsk]] Oblast. According to [[Marcel Erdal]], due to its particular characteristics, Siberian Tatar can be considered as a bridge between [[Kipchak languages|Kipchak]] and [[Siberian Turkic languages|Siberian]] Turkic languages. ==Dialects== Siberian Tatar consists of three dialects: [[Tobol-Irtysh Tatar dialect|Tobol-Irtysh]], [[Baraba Tatar dialect|Baraba or Tsanakül]] and [[Tom Tatar dialect|Tom or Umar-Tom]]. According to D. G. Tumasheva, the Baraba dialect is grammatically closest to the [[Southern Altai language|southern dialect of Altai]], [[Kyrgyz language|Kyrgyz]] and has significant grammatical similarities with [[Chulym language|Chulym]], [[Khakas language|Khakas]], [[Shor language|Shor]], and [[Tuvan language|Tuvan]]. The Tom dialect is, in her opinion, even closer to [[Altai languages|Altai]] and similar languages. The Tevriz sub-dialect of the Tobol-Irtysh dialect shares significant elements with the [[Siberian Turkic languages]], namely Altai, Khakas and Shor. Although [[Gabdulkhay Akhatov]] was a Volga Tatar, he immersed into studying of the phonetic peculiarities of Siberian Tatar language of the [[Indigenous peoples of Siberia|indigenous population of Siberia]], the Siberian Tatars. In his work "The Dialect of the West Siberian Tatars" (1963) Akhatov wrote about Tobol-Irtysh Siberian Tatars, a western group of Siberian Tatars, who are indigenous to the [[Omsk Oblast|Omsk]] and [[Tyumen Oblast|Tyumen]] Oblasts. In his work "Dialect of the West Siberian Tatars" (1963) [[Gabdulkhay Akhatov]] wrote about a territorial resettlement of the Tobol-Irtysh Tatars [[Tyumen Oblast|Tyumen]] and [[Omsk Oblast|Omsk]] areas. Subjecting a comprehensive integrated analysis of the phonetic system, the lexical composition and grammatical structure, the scientist concluded that the language of the Siberian Tatars is a separate language, it is divided into three dialects and it is one of the most ancient Turkic languages.[[Gabdulkhay Akhatov]]. The Dialect of the West Siberian Tatars. Ufa, 1963, 195 p. {{in lang|ru}} Professor G. Akhatov named Siberian Tatar dialects of Tyumen and Omsk Oblasts dialects of the West Siberian Tatars, while dialects of Baraba and Tom Tatars he named dialects of the East Siberian Tatars. Some works further differentiate sub-dialects of three aforementioned dialects, breaking them down as follows:{{Cite web |title=Сибирскотатарский язык {{!}} Малые языки России |url=https://minlang.iling-ran.ru/lang/sibirskotatarskiy-yazyk |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=minlang.iling-ran.ru}} * Tobol-Irtysh Tatar dialect ** Tyumen sub-dialect ([[Tyumensky District]], [[Yalutorovsky District]], and [[Nizhnetavdinsky District]] of Tyumen Oblast) ** Tobol sub-dialect ([[Tobolsky District]], [[Vagaysky District]], [[Yarkovsky District]] of Tyumen Oblast) *** Eastern Tobol (Tokuz-Uvat) variety (Vagaysky District) ** Zabolotny sub-dialect (Tobolsky District and Nizhnetavdinsky District of Tyumen Oblast) ** Tevriz (Kurdak, Kurtak) sub-dialect ([[Tevrizsky District]], [[Ust-Ishimsky District]], [[Znamensky District, Omsk Oblast|Znamensky District]] of Omsk Oblast, plus some settlements in Tyumen Oblast's Vagaysky District) ** Tara sub-dialect ([[Tarsky District]], [[Bolsherechensky District]], [[Kolosovsky District]] of Omsk Oblast) * Baraba Tatar dialect (spoken throughout the [[Baraba steppe]]) * Tom Tatar dialect ** Eushtino-Chatsk ([[Tomsky District]], Tomsk Oblast) *** Orsk Chat sub-dialect ([[Kolyvansky District]], Novosibirsk Oblast) ** Kalmak ([[Yurginsky District, Kemerovo Oblast]]) Baraba and Tom dialects of Siberian Tatar language belong to Kyrgyz–Kipchak subdivision of Turkic languages, together with Kyrgyz, Southern Altai, Teleut, and Telengit. Tobol-Irtysh dialect belongs to Kipchak–Nogai subdivision of Turkic languages, which also includes Nogai, Karagash, steppe dialect of Crimean Tatar, Kazakh, Karakalpak, and Kipchak dialects of Uzbek. ==Phonology== ===Vowels=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! rowspan="2" | !! colspan="2" | [[Front vowel|Front]] !! colspan="2" | [[Back vowel|Back]] |- !unrounded ![[Roundedness|rounded]] !unrounded ![[Roundedness|rounded]] |- !
